title: LLM-jp-4 Technical Report
data_curation: Strict reproducibility and licensing rules apply: only data at release levels L1-L3, and only open-source-licensed models for data construction (no GPT, Claude or Llama outputs). Datasets built with such models are rejected even if permissively licensed. This forced OSS rebuilds: FineWeb-Rescored re-annotates the 450K FineWeb-Edu documents with Qwen3-32B and scores all 24.5B FineWeb documents, and MegaMath-Web-Pro-Max-OSS (83M docs, 67.4B tokens) is rebuilt with gpt-oss-120b. Mid-training regenerates LLM-jp-Corpus-Midtraining-v1 with gpt-oss-120b. SFT targets (reasoning plus answer at low/medium/high effort) are synthesized by gpt-oss-120b from Nemotron, ichikara, WizardLM and other prompts, plus the new LLMC Math set (2,243 handwritten Japanese problems expanded to ~150K). SFT data is kept only when the judge gives 5/5 on all five quality dimensions. DPO pairs are max/min of 4 samples scored by a gpt-oss-120b judge.
curriculum: Each model is trained from scratch on ~12T tokens. Pre-training Phase 1 (6.3T tokens, LLM-jp Corpus v4) builds broad knowledge, with sampling weights from 13 small-scale 7.7B/400B-token runs. Phase 2 (4.2T tokens, Corpus v4.1) emphasizes math and code (The Stack v2, MMWPM-OSS), chosen via a 2^(5-2) fractional-factorial study. Mid-training (1.26T tokens) uses a 50:50 mix of instruction corpus and Phase 2 pretraining data at half the pretraining LR, extending context 4K → 16K → 64K (0.84T + 0.21T + 0.21T tokens). Post-training is SFT (2 epochs, ~10.83B tokens) then DPO (2 epochs), with no RL. All stages use WSD schedules with 1-sqrt decay to zero; Phase 1 decay branches were forked from the stable run.
method: Two models: an 8.6B dense LLaMA-2-style model and a 32.1B-total / 3.8B-active Qwen3-style MoE (wide-and-shallow, 128 experts with 8 active, QK-norm, router z-loss 1e-3, load-balance loss 1e-2, FP32 router). Both use GQA, a 196,608-token Unigram tokenizer (EN/JA/ZH/KO, split digits) and 64K context, and are trained with Megatron-LM on ABCI H200. Proxy studies found that only a smaller global batch (512) helped. The chat template is OpenAI Harmony with analysis and final channels and reasoning-effort control. SFT packs to fixed 64K chunks with AdamW (β2=0.98), peak LR 4e-5 and batch 64, upsampling AnswerCarefully 16x. DPO uses β=0.5 with summed (not length-normalized) log-probs, LR 9e-7 and batch 256. Pair filters: helpfulness top score >6 and gap ≥2; safety top score >3 and gap ≥1; chosen/rejected length ratio ≤1.5.
eval_metrics: llm-jp-eval v2.1.3 (Japanese and English category averages), plus MMLU, JMMLU, GPQA Diamond (EN/JA), AIME 2024/2025, HLE and BBH. LLM-as-a-Judge via llm-jp-judge uses a GPT-5.4 judge averaged over 3 runs, on MT-Bench JA/EN, AnswerCarefully v2.0 (336 questions) and llm-jp-instructions (400 questions). Baselines are llm-jp-3.1-8x13b-instruct4, Qwen3-8B and gpt-oss-20b. Japanese average: 0.590 (8B) and 0.605 (32B-A3B), vs 0.307 for the predecessor and 0.608 for Qwen3-8B. English: 0.634 / 0.650 vs Qwen3-8B 0.714. 32B-A3B scores: JMMLU 0.820, GPQA-JA 0.540, GPQA-EN 0.520, AIME24/25 0.400/0.300; medium-effort MT-Bench JA/EN 7.82/7.86.
key_results: LLM-jp-4-32B-A3B roughly doubles the previous generation's Japanese llm-jp-eval average (0.307 → 0.605) and matches Qwen3-8B (0.608) and gpt-oss-20b (0.604). At medium reasoning effort it beats gpt-oss-20b on MT-Bench JA (7.82 vs 7.33), AnswerCarefully (3.70 vs 3.55) and llm-jp-instructions (3.61 vs 3.16). It still trails both baselines on English, GPQA-EN and AIME.
evolution_note: Successor to LLM-jp-3/3.1 and a Japanese 'sovereign AI' counterpart to fully open efforts like OLMo, Pythia and Apertus. It reacts to license contamination in popular open datasets (FineWeb-Edu and MegaMath built with Llama) by rebuilding them with Apache-licensed models (Qwen3, gpt-oss). Its thinking post-training is SFT+DPO only, distilled from gpt-oss-120b in Harmony format without RL. It shows that OSAID-compliant, fully reproducible pipelines can reach parity with similar-scale open-weight models on Japanese tasks.
